title: Oscairn panel map version 1
description: How a non-MIDI device panel's 4-byte messages decode (devices/roland-fantom0's panel_reader.h, docs/fantom-0.md): where the kind, ID, value and encoder step sit in a message, and the control each kind and ID is. The first byte of every message has bit 7 set; the reader frames on it. Sections listed in estimated are guesses, not read off a unit.

kinds.description: The kind field's value for each message kind (Roland's PMDWEncoder, PMDWADChange, PMDWSwitchOn, PMDWSwitchOff); all different

analogId.description: An analog message's ID, where it is not where id is; default: id

value.description: An analog control's position, 0 to its max

analogMax.description: An analog control's top value, unless its entry says; default 1023

encoderStep.description: The change one encoder step makes, 0 to 1 across a target's range; default 1/127

analogDeadband.description: Steps: an analog control's same value again, or a turn back by this many or fewer short of either end, is chatter, which the engine does not play; a move on in one direction always plays; default 0, none

items.description: A control: its message kind and ID, and its identity (knob:N, fader:N, wheel:N, screen:N, button:N as overrides name them, RFC 0024), a pad of the Performance's pad map (pad:N, from 1) or a fixed control's profile function. Without an id it is not mapped yet and is skipped. No two entries of one kind share an id

kind.description: switch: both switch kinds, on and off

step.description: Encoder only: its change per step; negative turns it round

Field.description: A number from a message, one of two ways. bytes: the bytes (0 to 3) joined, most significant first, the low `bits` of each (default 8), shifted right by `shift`, masked by `mask`, and read as two's complement in the mask's width when `signed` (the mask then a run of low bits). parts: for a number whose bits are not the low bits of each byte, the parts joined, most significant first, and read as two's complement in their total width when `signed`

Part.description: `bits` bits of byte `byte`, from bit `shift` (default 0) up; they end within the byte
